documents_checked.document_title: Human research ethics institutional approval process
documents_checked.text:
Researchers must:
design and conduct their research in accordance with the Australian Code for the Responsible
Conduct of Research; and
ensure that their research is ethically reviewed, conducted and monitored in accordance with
the National Statement.
Human research must be reviewed and approved by the Human Research Ethics Committee
BEFORE the research may commence. Ethics approvals may not be granted retrospectively.
Sub-committees assist with low risk applications (Low-Risk Sub-Committee, Psychology and
Exercise Science Low-Risk Sub-Committee).
It is your responsibility to ensure that this National Statement is used in your research
proposals, application for ethics approval and ethics review
Commencing research without ethics approval is a breach of both the National Statement and
Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research.

case_summary.review_route_explanation: N075 provides general complaint handling, N241 provides research integrity allegation reporting, and N164 (7.1 -> N088) provides student appeals.

review_route_evidence.text:
This policy provides the University’s principles for the management of complaints in
relation to the University, a University education Agent, or related party where a
response or resolution is sought, expected or legally required.
This policy applies to all types of complaints, such as student appeals, and complaints
related to student integrity and employee conduct.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Synthetic responses distinguished from human empirical evidence, with an authorised research/ethics scope for the changed design.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: No policy in the Murdoch bundle explicitly requires synthetic AI-generated participant responses to be distinguished from human empirical evidence or mandates HREC scope amendment when AI simulation replaces approved human participants.
case_summary.case_note: Murdoch's human research ethics guidance (N242) mandates prior HREC approval under the National Statement and Australian Code (N172), while N087 (6.7.1) prohibits falsified or made-up data in coursework. However, Murdoch's Human Research Ethics Policy and Research Integrity Policy/Procedure are absent from the bundle, and no available rule addresses AI-simulated participant responses replacing human subjects, leaving a critical gap. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15, and this proposal awaits human verification.
